Which SDGs does my paper match?

Paste your title, abstract and author keywords. The checker runs them against Elsevier's search query for each of the 17 Sustainable Development Goals and shows which goals match, which part of each query your wording triggers, and what excluded it.

The checker isn't running in this viewer. This usually happens when the file is opened from WhatsApp, email or a phone's file preview, which don't run the checker. Open the file in a web browser such as Chrome, Safari, Edge or Firefox, or use the web link your school shared.

How to read the result

  • Scopus maps documents to SDGs by matching the record against these queries, plus a machine-learning step. This checker reproduces only the query part, so a match here is a strong sign, not a guarantee, and a paper the query misses can still be tagged.
  • Elsevier states that it does not support running these queries in Scopus Advanced Search. Use this page to check your wording, not to count SDG papers.
  • Matching ignores capital letters, accents, hyphens and punctuation, and treats * as a wildcard. Plurals count only where the query lists them. Terms in braces, such as {ODA}, must appear exactly as written. Proximity rules (W/n, PRE/n) count the words between the two terms.
  • Some rules also look at Scopus index keywords, which you cannot supply here, so Scopus may include or exclude a record differently.
  • The theme names for each part of a query are descriptive labels based on the terms in that part. They are not Elsevier's names. The SDG 10 and SDG 16 queries are single keyword lists, so their matches are shown together.
  • Nothing you type leaves your browser.
